constraint_review: Mass 46 kg including battery versus 60 kg limit is met with 14 kg margin on a named sum. Stowed 0.90 m by 0.42 m by 0.45 m versus 1.0 m by 0.5 m by 0.5 m box is met, deployed growth to 1.05 m length and 0.68 m track is allowed as unfolding. BP-1 digging is met in analysis by 11 N kerf draft versus 294 N traction. Blind operation out of sight and hearing is met by onboard cameras with wireless link plus heartbeat stop and fiducial reset.
feedback:
Overall this is a workable blind digger that I would release to detail design. The working principle holds as a load path and a signal path: a narrow front chain loosens a shallow slot, a wider bucket ladder lifts the loose spoil, a steep hopper stores it, and a rear tilt plus floor screw meters it over the bin while cameras and a heartbeat stop allow driving without seeing the machine. My main worry is flow out of the 20 L wedge through the 150 mm outlet in cohesive BP-1, followed by tooth wear and tip margin if ever run full, but none breaks physics. Compared with the closest prior art, the Chondrobot-2 four-wheel bucket-ladder tele-robotic miner with 8 kg per min and 18 kg collector, this keeps the same archetype but splits cut then lift with a 100 mm kerf in front of a wide ladder and replaces single-bucket tipping with a live-bottom screw plus rear pivot, plus folding arms for the box.

Every function has a means and the chief designer's choices close the gaps. Traverse has four rigid grouser wheels on folding arms, loosen has the narrow kerf chain, collect and lift has the inclined bucket ladder, contain has the 20 L steep wedge hopper, discharge has the tilt screw, and blind coordination has the three-camera set with wireless link to a sealed operator plus heartbeat stop and fiducial reset. No function is left without a part and the closing synthesis fixes leading dig end and trailing dump end, so there is no missing function. The meeting closed with no open objections and all four leads ready, so the concept is settled subject only to normal detail checks.

Cutting and traction use the right regime. The board uses a Balovnev-type shallow cut with cohesion plus weight terms, force equals width times cohesion times depth plus one-half density times gravity times depth squared times a factor, which is the correct form for a 50 mm deep scraper in loose frictional soil. Recomputing with the board inputs gives 0.30 m times 500 Pa times 0.05 m plus 0.5 times 1500 kg per cu m times 9.81 m per sq s times 0.0025 sq m times 4.6 equals 32.9 N for full width in the shallow cut estimate (E9), scaled by 0.10 over 0.30 to 11.0 N for the kerf (E64). Earth weight for 60 kg is 589 N in the weight calculation (E22). Available traction of 294 N in the tip-over and stopping check (E23) is about one-half weight for grousers on loose soil and gives a margin of about 27 times over the 11 N kerf draft and 8.9 times even over full-width draft, so drive can hold the cut. Power as force times chain speed is the right relation. The board computes 32.9 N times 0.5 m per s equals 16.4 W ladder power (E59), which conservatively uses full-width force; the kerf-corrected value would be 11 N times 0.5 m per s equals 5.5 W, so the board overstates dig power and remains safe. Dig energy per 15 kg trip as power times fill time is 16.45 W times 112 s over 3600 equals 0.512 Wh in the trip energy calculation (E60), tiny against the 24 V times 20 Ah equals 480 Wh pack, about a laptop battery, and even with 200 W drive plus compute the 25 min mixed-duty use is near 100 Wh, so energy closes with large margin. Fill in 112 s to 15 kg at 8 kg per min in the fill simulation (E11) is consistent with Chondrobot rates.

Bearing, mass, size and stiffness close. Ground pressure as weight over four contact patches is the right model. Recomputing with the board patch of 0.15 m by 0.063 m gives 589 N over 0.0378 sq m equals 15,600 Pa or 15.6 kPa in the pressure calculation (E25), about one-half a person standing on one foot and reasonable for loose sand. The deployed simulation (E51) uses 0.12 m wheel width instead of 0.15 m, which recomputes to 19.5 kPa, still low, but the width inconsistency should be unified in detail design. Mass sums to 46.0 kg in the updated mass sum (E62) and the named-terms sum (E68) as 9 plus 10 plus 8 plus 4.5 plus 3 plus 6 plus 2.5 plus 3 equals 46 kg, about an adult, versus the 60 kg limit with 14 kg margin in the margin check (E67), so the mass limit is shown by addition, not words. Hopper payload as density times volume is 1500 kg per cu m times 0.02 cu m equals 30 kg maximum (E10), run half-full at 15 kg per the fill simulation (E11), about a bag of soil. Stowed envelope of 0.90 m by 0.42 m by 0.45 m fits the 1.0 m by 0.5 m by 0.5 m box in the deployed versus stowed simulation (E51) and the folding-chassis sketch (E24), with deployed length 1.05 m and track 0.68 m allowed after start. Frame stiffness as cantilever tip sag equals load times length cubed over three times modulus times second moment is the right beam model. Second moment for two 25.4 mm square tubes with 3 mm wall as outer fourth minus inner fourth over 12 times two recomputes to 4.58e-08 m4 in the tube calculation (E61), and sag for 300 N on 0.5 m with 68.9 GPa gives 37.5 over 9467 equals 0.00396 m or 3.96 mm in the sag calculation (E63), acceptable at concept and buildable in TIG-welded 6061-T6 tube with 15 ksi working stress.

Blind-operation safety uses the right kinematics. Brake-only stop as velocity squared over twice deceleration gives 0.25 over 4 equals 0.0625 m at 0.5 m per s and 2 m per sq s in the stopping check (E23). With 0.5 s heartbeat loss the coast of 0.25 m plus brake gives 0.3125 m, essentially the 0.308 m total with link loss in the watchdog simulation (E32), a desk-step, so the fail-safe holds. Drift bounded to 0.10 to 0.15 m with 5 m fiducial reset in the drift simulation (E33) and final align to 0.03 to 0.04 m at 1 to 2 m in the align budget (E58) plausibly puts the 150 mm outlet over a 0.4 m bin mouth. Dump clearance of 0.15 m from a 0.55 m pivot over a 0.40 m lip in the tip and clearance simulation (E51) and tip factor 1.69 level-only at 15 kg are plausible, but worst case was not shown full at 30 kg or on a slope, so detail design must gate dumping by tilt sensor and interlock half-full trips as the team already intends.

Material, energy and signal flows trace end to end without gaps. Soil goes kerf slot to side spoil rows to wide ladder pickup in the kerf sketch (E65) to gravity chute to hopper in the side-view sketch (E13) to screw to rear outlet to bin, with positions front to rear consistent. Energy goes lithium phosphate pack through a fused bus to dig, drive, tilt and cameras, and signal goes downward dig camera optically to onboard encoder to radio to remote screens in the stated measurement chain. The outlet area of pi times 0.15 m squared over 4 equals 0.0177 sq m in the outlet calculation (E69) is arithmetic-correct but does not prove mass flow; the steep-wall claim rests on unopened hopper-flow and BP-1 sources (E3)(E7)(E8) and cohesion 500 Pa was never read from an opened page, so it is weaker than the opened Moonraker, e-stop and odometry sources (E14)(E27)(E28). That missing Jenike analysis does not defeat the concept because a live screw plus tilt can force metered discharge, and the team correctly carries half-full operation and current-limit backout, but the calculation should be done on paper in detail design. Other deviations are minor: ladder power uses full-width force while traction margin claims kerf force, wheel width is 0.15 m in one calc and 0.12 m in another, and mass moved from 47 kg to 46 kg as the frame stiffened, none of which changes acceptance. The machine is buildable with purchasable chain, grouser wheels, smooth steel hopper, 24 V pack, cameras and ordinary welding and bolting, with arching, edge wear and tag visibility left as named bench checks after build, which is proper for concept stage.

I keep accept with no further evidence requests. The two items I previously listed are detail-design advice, not blocks to the working principle or to a stated limit: do a Jenike critical outlet and wall-angle computation for BP-1 versus the 150 mm outlet with screw assist to size the outlet and wall, and draw a summed stowed width and height build-up with frame plus folded arms plus wheels and rotation gaps against the 0.5 m limits to unify the 0.12 m versus 0.15 m wheel width.
